newsitem.title: SPAIN: Telefonica seen favouring MCI in US.
newsitem.headline: Telefonica seen favouring MCI in US.

text.p: Telefonica de Espana is likely to opt for a new U.S. deal with MCI Communications Corp, attracted not only by its strong home market position but also by its powerful European ally, British Telecom.
"At the moment I would bet on MCI and BT," said an analyst at Ibersecurities in Madrid.

Telefonica is searching for an inroad into the United States and it has a number of willing suitors given its extensive Latin American holdings through international subisidary TISA, which had sales last year of 350 billion pesetas.

But Telefonica is also clearly weighing its strategic options well beyond the U.S., where the two main rivals for a link-up, MCI and AT&T Corp, have secure market positions, analysts said. Telefonica already has an alliance with AT&T.
"MCI would give Telefonica access to the U.S. where it is a key operator. But AT&T could also provide that access," a Madrid-based analyst said.
"But this is not just about U.S. access, Telefonica's talks imply it is reviewing its entire system of alliances...to allow them to expand in the future," he added.

On Thursday, Telefonica -- which is halfway through its self-imposed deadline of six weeks to select a U.S. partner -- said its board had met to discuss international alliances a day earlier, but that it had yet to make a decision.
"It's true that the board met yesterday to study the issue of an international partner, but it wasn't the only subject and we haven't made any decision yet," the spokesman told Reuters.
In a statement published by the stock market commission CNMV, Telefonica said it might finalise talks in coming days.
Telefonica Chairman Juan Villalonga has said the group was in talks with the chairmen of MCI, BT, Southwestern Bell Corp as well as with AT&T with whom it already has an alliance.
AT&T directs the primarily European consortium of Unisource, which groups Sweden's Telia, Swiss Telecom and Koninklijke pTT Nederland as well as Telefonica.

MCI is hooked up with AT&T's key rival, BT. Concert, their planned merger, could offer Telefonica better European growth than Unisource, which analysts say has not provided Telefonica with huge benefits.

"Doing an alliance with MCI would also mean one with BT, which is the most competitive group at the moment. It would also remove one of Telefonica's key European rivals," another Madrid-based analyst said.
